entities.name: OCLC, Inc.
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
OCLC, Inc., founded on July 5, 1967, in Dublin, Ohio, represents a pivotal evolution in library science through its establishment of a global library cooperative model. Initially initiated by a consortium of libraries, OCLC was driven by the vision of its first president, Dr. Frederick G. Kilgour, who sought to enhance bibliographic organization and information sharing among libraries, thereby addressing the inefficiencies of cataloging and resource management across the United States and beyond. This cooperative framework not only transformed library operations but also established a standard for interlibrary cooperation that has influenced library practices worldwide.

The organization developed the WorldCat database, which became the world's largest library catalog, containing over 500 million bibliographic records from libraries across the globe. This monumental achievement has enabled libraries to share resources more effectively, promoting access to information and fostering a culture of collaboration. By digitizing and cataloging vast amounts of library data, OCLC has played a crucial role in the transition from physical to digital resources, responding to the changing landscape of information consumption in the late 20th and early 21st centuries.

As a result of OCLC's initiatives, libraries have been able to enhance their services, leading to a more informed public and improved educational resources. The cooperative model has inspired similar organizations worldwide, promoting the democratization of information access and supporting academic and public libraries in their mission to serve diverse communities. The impact of OCLC can be seen today in the continued evolution of library services, particularly as they adapt to technological advancements and the increasing demand for digital resources.
